newsitem.title: ITALY: Milan set to unveil latest in fashion finesse.
newsitem.headline: Milan set to unveil latest in fashion finesse.

text.p: Milanese finesse takes the lead on the international fashion circuit next week when Italian designers slip the wraps off their autumn/winter 1997/98 women's ready-to-wear collections.

Italy's established design names like Giorgio Armani and Gianni Versace follow hard on the heels of London's more avant-garde fashion week and are set to offer the luxury and sophistication for which they are famed.

"The collections in Milan are more grown up. When you talk about London you talk about avant-garde use, wild mixes and cutting edge design," said Mary Gallagher, European consultant at exclusive London store Harvey Nichols.
"In Milan it tends to be much more sophistication and luxury -- the utmost in pure luxury, with fine fabrics and beautiful tailoring," Gallagher told Reuters by telephone from Paris.
But Italian designers say times are changing and with them consumer attitudes.

Armani, whose modern classicism is a central pillar of contemporary Italian style, said in a recent magazine interview that fashion and its consumers had altered since the Italian designers' heady rise of the 1980s.
"Fashion isn't dead, it's just changed," he told Panorama news weekly earlier this month.
"Up to the mid Sixties there was French high fashion and the rest followed. Then in the mid Seventies the Japanese arrived in Paris, in the Eighties there was the Italian ready-to-wear boom.
"Today there's a great choice. Different trends can co-exist," he said.

Versace, another stylist whose name is a by-word for Italian glamour, noted the need to evolve along with clients, telling the daily Corriere della Sera recently: "It's time to talk about the real role of the designer.

"With so much standardisation of styles, trends, models, photographers, you feel displaced, you have to ask yourself who you are working for. You have to deal with a new kind of woman and take more notice of the feelings of ordinary people."

Versace said much had changed in the last few years. "Women have gloried in their beauty, their sexuality, their professionality...But today they are concentrating on quality, on a discreet femininity. There's no middle way.
"By day they want to dress in a simple and practical way. It's only for the evening that they are looking for rich clothes, but with sobriety."

Both stylists present their main collections at the tail end of the week, with Versace showing at his elegant palazzo just off Milan's exclusive Via Monte Napoleone on March 8 and Armani as usual ending the week on Sunday.
Although the shows start this Sunday, the big guns of Italian fashion will not start rolling out until Wednesday when designer Krizia unveils her collection.
She is followed on Thursday by Emporio Armani, the silver-haired designer's youthful second line, and fashion house Gucci, who name is synonymous with suave Italian luxury.
Friday boasts German Jil Sander, fashion duo Domenico Dolce and Stefano Gabbana, Gianfranco Ferre and style house Prada.
